block.name: Everything you need, out of the box

MetaData.title: Exponential: open source content management, built to last
MetaData.description: Exponential 6.0.15 is an open source CMS and web application platform: front-end editing, flexible page layouts, five databases and a built-in web server.

MetaData.title: Platform: what Exponential 6.0.15 brings
MetaData.description: The features of Exponential 6.0.15: front-end editing, page layouts, the Velocity server, design tokens, five databases, security and the help center.

ezobject:attribute.name: Title
ezobject:attribute.text: Edit the page you are looking at

section.paragraph: The website sidebar puts editing, creating and moving content on the page itself. Editors stay on the site they are building and never lose their place.

Sign in and a slim tab appears at the edge of every page. Open it and the sidebar offers what the page allows you to do: edit this article, add a page below it, move it, hide it, or schedule the next version. The administration is one click away, but most days you will not need it.

section.header: Built for the people who write

li.paragraph: Edit in place. The edit form opens on the page you came from and returns you there when you publish.
Create where you are. New articles, events and images go straight into the section you are browsing.
Schedule. Publish at a set time and take a page down again, through the same scheduling the administration uses.
Your account. Change your password, set up a second factor and see your drafts from the sidebar.

section.header: Only for the people who need it
section.paragraph: Visitors never see the sidebar. New installations grant it to the Administrator and Editor roles only, and every action checks the same permissions as the administration.

MetaData.title: Edit the page you are looking at
MetaData.description: The website sidebar puts editing, creating and moving content on the page itself. Editors stay on the site they are building and never lose their place.

ezobject:attribute.name: Title
ezobject:attribute.text: Pages built from zones and blocks

section.paragraph: Frontpages are made of zones and blocks. Pick a layout, drop in a hero, a feature grid, the latest news or a poll, and publish. No developer needed.

This very site is built that way. Every section front, including the one you came from, is a frontpage with a zone layout. Each zone holds blocks, and each block either shows items an editor picked by hand or fetches the newest content of a section on its own.

section.header: Blocks that come with the site

li.paragraph: Main story for a hero with a large image and a call to action.
2, 3, 4 and 5 items for feature grids, teasers and testimonials.
Latest content and keyword blocks that keep themselves up to date.
Gallery and multimedia carousel for photos.
Poll, tag cloud, search and feed reader for the side of the page.

section.paragraph: Items can be queued to appear at a set time. The timeline in the administration shows how a page will look on any day, so a campaign can be prepared on Monday and go live on Friday on its own.
For larger sites, Exponential Layouts adds rule-based layouts, shared headers and footers and a visual layout editor on top of the same idea.

MetaData.title: Pages built from zones and blocks
MetaData.description: Frontpages are made of zones and blocks. Pick a layout, drop in a hero, a feature grid, the latest news or a poll, and publish. No developer needed.

ezobject:attribute.name: Title
ezobject:attribute.text: Velocity: the web server is part of the product

section.paragraph: As of 6.0.15 every installation comes with Velocity, a persistent-worker web and application server written for Exponential. Pages that used to be built from scratch on every request start warm.

Velocity keeps the kernel loaded between requests, so a page costs only what it really does. It serves HTTPS with its own certificates, compresses and caches static files, resizes images, and answers repeat visitors from its response cache.

li.paragraph: A persistent worker pool with a warm-up, so the first visitor after a deploy is not the slow one.
HTTPS with automatic certificates, HTTP/2 and precompressed static files.
WebSockets, server-sent events and rooms for live features.
A scheduler, a control panel and one command to deploy a change: exp:velocity deploy.

section.paragraph: Velocity is the recommended engine for every stage. FrankenPHP is the production-ready alternative, and Apache or nginx with PHP-FPM keep working exactly as before.

MetaData.title: Velocity: the web server is part of the product
MetaData.description: As of 6.0.15 every installation comes with Velocity, a persistent-worker web and application server written for Exponential. Pages that used to be built from scratch on every request start warm.

ezobject:attribute.name: Title
ezobject:attribute.text: Design tokens, dark mode and modern templates

section.paragraph: Colors, type and spacing come from one set of design tokens. Every page follows the reader's light or dark preference, and the motion respects reduced-motion settings.

The site designs were rebuilt for 6.0.15. They are responsive from phone to wide screen, accessible to WCAG 2.2 AA, and fast: no render-blocking fonts, images sized for the screen, and scripts loaded as modules after the page.

section.header: Templates the way you like them
section.paragraph: Exponential templates work as they always have, and the same views can also be written in Smarty or Twig. Overrides keep their keys, so a site built years ago keeps working while you modernize it one template at a time.
Pages pass a strict Content Security Policy: no inline styles, no inline scripts and no inline event handlers. The JavaScript is vanilla ES modules on top of the shared UI components.

MetaData.title: Design tokens, dark mode and modern templates
MetaData.description: Colors, type and spacing come from one set of design tokens. Every page follows the reader's light or dark preference, and the motion respects reduced-motion settings.

section.paragraph: Run Exponential on MySQL or MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MongoDB or Oracle. The content model, the templates and the extensions stay the same.

SQLite gets a site running in seconds with nothing to set up, which makes it ideal for trying things out and for small sites. MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL carry most production sites. MongoDB and Oracle fit into the infrastructure many large organizations already run.

li.paragraph: One installer command for every engine: exp:install --db=sqlite, --db=pgsql and so on.
The same site packages install on all five.
Extensions create their tables on every engine when they are switched on.

MetaData.title: Five databases, one content model
MetaData.description: Run Exponential on MySQL or MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MongoDB or Oracle. The content model, the templates and the extensions stay the same.

ezobject:attribute.name: Title
ezobject:attribute.text: Security your editors will actually use

section.paragraph: Two-factor sign-in, "Verify it's you" before sensitive changes, a strict Content Security Policy and an audit trail, switched on without extra work.

Security that gets in the way gets switched off. Exponential keeps it simple: a second factor on the sign-in form, a short check before a password or a role changes, and sessions that end everywhere else when a password does.

li.paragraph: Time-based one-time passwords on the web sign-in.
"Verify it's you" for changes to accounts, roles and settings.
A Content Security Policy that every shipped page passes.
An audit trail of who changed what, and when.
Forwarded headers trusted only from proxies you configure.

MetaData.title: Security your editors will actually use
MetaData.description: Two-factor sign-in, "Verify it's you" before sensitive changes, a strict Content Security Policy and an audit trail, switched on without extra work.

ezobject:attribute.name: Title
ezobject:attribute.text: A help center inside the product

section.paragraph: Every screen of the administration links to its help page, and the whole manual installs with the site, in English and German.

The help center is content like any other: concepts, tasks, references and troubleshooting topics, organized into manuals for editors, developers, designers and administrators. It is searchable, it works offline on an intranet, and you can add your own pages for your team.

li.paragraph: Context links from the administration to the right topic.
Manuals for every audience, from first steps to extension development.
Your own house rules, written next to the official pages.

section.paragraph: The same manuals are online at doc.exponential.earth.

MetaData.title: A help center inside the product
MetaData.description: Every screen of the administration links to its help page, and the whole manual installs with the site, in English and German.

ezobject:attribute.name: Title
ezobject:attribute.text: Upgrades and migrations in one command

section.paragraph: The console checks what is pending, backs up, updates the code and the database, and verifies the site afterward. A rollback is one command away.
Upgrading a content management system used to be a weekend project. With Exponential it is a command you can run on a Tuesday afternoon.

li.paragraph: exp:upgrade:status shows what is done and what is pending, and changes nothing.
exp:upgrade --apply backs up, updates and checks the site.
Content migrations are recorded, replayed and rolled back with exp:migration.

section.paragraph: Sites that started on eZ Publish, the system Exponential grew out of, upgrade along the same path.

MetaData.title: Upgrades and migrations in one command
MetaData.description: The console checks what is pending, backs up, updates the code and the database, and verifies the site afterward. A rollback is one command away.

section.paragraph: Publish fast, schedule campaigns, and keep every story, photo and correction under version control.
Editors write on the page, photo desks upload in bulk, and section fronts update themselves from the latest stories. The timeline lets the homepage for tomorrow morning be planned tonight.

li.paragraph: Frontpages built from blocks, scheduled ahead.
Full version history and preview of every draft.
RSS, podcasts and structured data for search engines.

Public websites must work for everyone. The site designs meet WCAG 2.2 AA, forms collect requests without third-party services, and the data stays on your own servers in the database you already run.

Roles and sections that mirror your departments.
Hosting on your own infrastructure, including Oracle.

Multi-site setups share content where it makes sense and keep it apart where it should be. Each faculty gets its own siteaccess, design and editors, while course information and news flow from one source.

li.paragraph: Many sites, one installation.
Events calendars for open days and lectures.
Single sign-on through the login handlers you already use.

Volunteers edit on the page without training, newsletters go out from the same content, and polls and feedback forms keep members involved. Everything is open source under the GPL, so the budget goes to the mission.

li.paragraph: Newsletters with subscriptions and consent.
Events, polls and forums.
No license fees, ever.

Run Exponential behind your firewall on SQLite or the database your IT team prefers. Teams own their sections, notifications tell people when a page they follow changes, and the help center pattern works just as well for your own handbooks.

Notifications and subscriptions.

ezobject:attribute.text: Exponential 6.0.15 brings the web server into the product

section.paragraph: The 6.0.15 line ships Velocity with every installation, rebuilt site designs, the website sidebar and support for five databases.
Four months of work went into 6.0.15. The headline is Velocity: the persistent-worker web server is now part of every installation, so a new site is fast from the first request.

li.paragraph: Velocity web and application server, included and recommended.
The website sidebar for front-end editing, in place of the old toolbar.
Modern site designs with design tokens and dark mode.
MongoDB and Oracle next to MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite.
One-command installation and upgrades.

ezobject:attribute.text: The Exponential Foundation opens its membership

section.paragraph: Companies and individuals who build on Exponential can now join the foundation and help steer the roadmap.

The Exponential Foundation looks after the project: its code, its name and its community. Membership is open to anyone who builds on Exponential, from freelancers to agencies to the organizations that run it in production.

Members propose and vote on roadmap themes, take part in release planning and get early access to release candidates. Contributions of code, translations and documentation count as much as sponsorship.

Translation waves over the summer brought dozens of new languages to the administration, the extensions and the help center. Right-to-left languages get mirrored layouts automatically.
Every translation is reviewed against a language guide, so terms stay consistent from the sign-in page to the last error message.

ezobject:attribute.name: Title
ezobject:attribute.text: Docker images and binaries for every platform

section.paragraph: Velocity now ships as Docker images and single-file binaries, so a test installation is one command on any machine.
Start a container, open the browser, and the setup is done. The images carry PHP, Velocity and the kernel; your site, its database and its storage live in volumes you control.
For servers without Docker, single-file binaries carry the same stack for Linux, macOS and Windows.

ezobject:attribute.name: Title
ezobject:attribute.text: Accessibility review of the site designs

section.paragraph: The site designs were reviewed against WCAG 2.2 AA: keyboard paths, focus, contrast, motion and screen-reader labels.

Every page now has a skip link, visible focus, landmarks and labels for its controls. Colors meet the contrast minimums in both light and dark mode, and animations stop when the reader asks for reduced motion.
If you find a barrier, please report it on the project's issue tracker; accessibility issues are treated as bugs.

ezobject:attribute.name: Title
ezobject:attribute.text: Typography that reads well on every screen

section.paragraph: Good typography is mostly restraint. Pick one family for text, set a comfortable measure of 60 to 75 characters, and give lines room to breathe. The new site designs use a fluid type scale: headings grow with the viewport, body text stays readable.

li.paragraph: Use the system font stack unless the brand truly needs a web font. It loads instantly and looks native.
Scale headings with clamp(), never with breakpoints alone.
Check contrast in dark mode too. Pure white on pure black glares; soften both.

section.paragraph: Before optimizing anything, measure. With Velocity's profile view you can see how much of a page is the kernel, how much is your templates and how much is the database.
In our measurements the biggest win was almost never clever code. It was caching the right blocks, sizing images for the screen they are shown on, and loading scripts after the content.

section.paragraph: Who makes Exponential, how it is governed and where it came from.
Exponential is open source software, maintained by the Exponential Foundation with 7x as its lead developer and supported by a worldwide community.

section.paragraph: The Exponential Foundation looks after the code, the name and the community of Exponential, so the project stays open for the long run.
The foundation holds the project's trademarks and infrastructure, organizes releases and community events, and makes sure Exponential stays free software under the GNU General Public License.

li.paragraph: Sets the release schedule and keeps the long-term support lines alive.

section.paragraph: 7x maintains the Exponential kernel, the extensions and the Velocity server, and offers hosting, support and development for organizations that run it.

7x has worked with this code base for many years and leads its development today: the 6.0 line, the modern site designs, the website sidebar and Velocity all came out of that work, together with the community.
The source code is on GitHub at github.com/se7enxweb, and the company is at se7enx.com.

MetaData.title: 7x, lead developer of Exponential
MetaData.description: 7x maintains the Exponential kernel, the extensions and the Velocity server, and offers hosting, support and development for organizations that run it.

section.paragraph: Exponential continues a code base with more than two decades of history. Here is how it got here.

The code base began life as eZ Publish, an open source content management system first released by eZ Systems in 1999. Its fourth generation was used by newspapers, governments and universities around the world.

When the original vendor moved on to a new platform, the community kept the legacy line alive. 7x took over its maintenance, brought it to modern PHP, and the project was renamed Exponential to mark a fresh start under the Exponential Foundation.
Today Exponential runs on PHP 8.0 to 8.5, ships its own web server, and keeps the content model and templates that so many sites were built on.
